title: Beyond Gene Co-Expression Modules: Meta-Module Organization and Oncogenic Signaling Associations in Colon Cancer
content: Bulk transcriptomic studies in colon cancer have primarily focused on molecular subtyping and prognostic gene signatures. While these approaches have refined tumor classification, they provide limited insight into the higher-order organization of oncogenic programs that shape tumor behavior. This study performs systems-level analysis to define the hierarchical architecture of transcriptional networks in colon cancer and identify functional axes that characterize tumor biology and may have clinical significance. Transcriptomics data were downloaded from TCGA-COAD for 458 colon cancer patients. We performed differential RNA-sequencing (DESeq2) analysis, followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). We integrated network topology, functional clustering and module organization to identify higher-order transcriptional axes. Transcriptomics data were integrated with clinical parameters. Tumor tissue showed proliferation-associated modules and enhanced immune network connectivity. Co-expression analysis identified four major functional axes defining its systems-level architecture: proliferative oncogenic signaling, metabolism, stromal organization and invasion, and immune responses. The proliferative and stromal axes were aassociated with advanced disease, whereas immune-related modules correlated with favorable clinical outcomes. The association was weak, but showed consistent directional pattern. Colon tumorigenesis appears to involve a coordinated transition between distinct network states characterized by the emergence of coordinated functional programs rather than isolated pathway activation. Systems-level immune and oncogenic polarization axes may provide a framework to understand clinical heterogeneity and to design biologically grounded network approaches.
